newsitem.title: UK: Seascope says UK listing to value it at 15 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Seascope says UK listing to value it at 15 mln stg.

text.p: UK tanker broker Seascope Shipping Holdings said on Thursday it expects the group to be valued at around 15 million sterling ($25 million) when it is listed on the London Stock exchange.
The placing is expected to raise around 4 million stg, Seascope said. Funds would be used to repay existing debt and preferred capital of 2.25 million stg and provide cash flow for investment.
Seascope, which issued a pathfinder prospectus today, said its share price range would be fixed on Thursday or Friday of next week.
A full prospectus giving details of a notional historic dividend for 1996 will be included in a full prospectus to be published later this month, Seascope said.
Seascope was formed 25 years ago but the present company was set up in 1992 by a management buyout from Henry Ansbacher Holdings Ltd.
The company reported pre-tax profits of 1.8 million stg on turnover of 6.6 million stg for the year ended December 31, 1996.
It said today that interim results for the six months to June 30, 1997 showed a pre-tax profit of 1.4 million stg on turnover of 4.3 million stg.

Chairman Tom Young said Seascope saw expansion and acquisition opportunities in the developing offshore oil exploration and production markets. Profit growth was also possible from the currently strong tanker markets, he said.
"The offshore business will continue to expand way beyond the North Sea and will not be as cyclical in nature as shipping," Young said.
He pointed to reducing wellhead costs and increasing world oil consumption as causes for the development of offshore drilling off West Africa, Brazil and south east Asia.
Seascope has built up its offshore experience since acquiring Aberdeen-based Jacobs Offshore Ltd in 1992.
Young added: "There is a need to rebuild the world's tanker fleet with only 20 percent currently being double hulled."

"Incidents like the oil spill in Tokyo Bay last week will increase the need for double hull vessels, particularly trading into sensitive areas like Japan and South Korea which have important fish farming industries," he said.

Seascope has developed a newbuilding section within its ships sales and purchase division which has been able to broker deals between ship owners and shipyards, particularly Japanese and Korean shipbuilders which have reduced their European sales presence.
The company takes a 1 percent commission on the price of such deals. The price of a new VLCC currently averages around $85 million.
Seascope is currently owned 53 percent by its staff and management and 40 percent by investment bank 3i, with a further 7 percent held by other investors.
The issue is being sponsored by Guinness Mahon & Co Ltd and Bell Lawrie White & Co is broker.
